profile.campus: Durham, Research Triangle Park, North Carolina (CyrusOne DUR1-DUR2)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility page, this Research Triangle Park campus at 2223 NE Creek Pkwy, Durham, NC 27713 publishes 40 MW and 420,000 sq ft combined across two buildings: DUR1, the existing building with 92,320 sq ft of raised floor across eleven data halls, and DUR2, a shell building CyrusOne describes as delivered in 2025 with capacity not yet broken out separately.

CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, was purchased by Cincinnati Bell for $525 million in 2010, completed an IPO in January 2013, and was taken private when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) closed a roughly $15 billion acquisition in March 2022. Durham's Research Triangle Park location places this campus in a market anchored by major research universities (Duke, UNC, NC State) and a dense biotech/pharma/tech corridor rather than a single hyperscale anchor tenant.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus publishes 40 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet in two buildings, accounting for 80 percent of North Carolina's disclosed data center power capacity.

The facility consists of DUR1, an operational building with 92,320 square feet of raised floor across eleven data halls, and DUR2, a shell building delivered in 2025 with no capacity yet specified. At standard colocation density of 95 watts per square foot, this footprint could hold roughly 400 racks, though AI training workloads typically require substantially higher power density and would reduce that count significantly. The operator publishes no information about electrical infrastructure, cooling capability, or accelerator support for either building.

Durham sits within Research Triangle Park, a region with established technology infrastructure and university proximity. The presence of a recently completed shell building suggests potential for expansion, but whether DUR2 will be equipped for modern accelerator workloads or remains speculatively leased is not disclosed. The campus's relevance to AI compute scaling depends entirely on power supply capability and cooling design, neither of which the operator has published.

North Carolina has nineteen mapped data centers, but only five disclose power figures totaling 50 MW. This Durham cluster's dominance of published state capacity reflects operator transparency rather than actual footprint, leaving the true power base in the state unknown.
